question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The possible side effects of these, when used externally on the (skin, include burning and itching of) the skin.

options.text: skin, including burning and itching of
skin, includes burning and itching of
skin, can include burning and itching off

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct as given because the subject "**effects**" is plural, which requires the plural verb "**include**."
 
• The parenthetical or descriptive phrase "**when used externally on the skin**" does not change the number of the main subject.
 
• The preposition "**of**" in "itching of the skin" is the correct usage to denote the location or source of the sensation.
 
• Therefore, **no correction is required**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The possible side effects of these, when used externally on the **skin, include burning and itching of** the skin."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Using "**including**" would turn the verb into a present participle, leaving the sentence without a main finite verb to support the subject "effects."
 
• **Option 2:** "**Includes**" is a singular verb form and would result in a subject-verb agreement error with the plural subject "effects."
 
• **Option 3:** "**Itching off**" is an incorrect prepositional usage; "off" implies removal or distance, whereas "of" correctly relates the itching to the skin.
